lines.text: Your friend is always two minutes away, for a reason you'd never guess.
Arjun lost twelve mornings to it.
He drives. Priya rides. One lane over.
Every morning he texts, outside. She replies, two minutes.
Two minutes, definition one: ten minutes. Fair.
Definition two: twenty five. The guard starts a stopwatch.
Definition three: forty. The guard brings Arjun a pillow.
So Arjun tries the oldest trick: lying about the time.
Pickup's at seven forty, he says. She strolls out at eight twenty.
Seven twenty. Eight twenty. Six a.m. Eight twenty.
Morning twelve, he sends a test. The car is on fire.
Reply. Two minutes.
It's an auto reply. She never read one fake time.
She's not late. She's asleep. Her phone's just polite.
Turns out, two minutes is a feeling, not a location.
So they switch to an app. Priya taps at pickup only from the actual gate.
Till then she watches Arjun's car on the live map. Metres, not minutes.
No texts. No horn. No pillow.
The auto reply still runs. Her boss just asked for the report. Two minutes.
Friend stuck on two minutes? Try Sahyatri. Link in bio.
